title: Is Die Hard A Christmas Movie? The Age-Old Question Has Arrived Just In Time | Explainers News - News18
text: As the world gears up for a cosy Christmas holiday season to spend time with their loved ones, cook hearty meals, share a drink too many, and watch movies together, they will also (once again) try to settle the age-old question. Yes, it’s that time of the year. Finally. Die Hard , a 1988 cult classic action movie, directed by John McTiernan, has everything on offer. There’s romance, there’s family, there’s Alan Rickman, and there’s action. Plenty of it. And there’s this never-ending raging debate: Is Die Hard a Christmas movie? NYPD detective John McClane lands in Los Angeles on Christmas Eve in a bid to reconcile with his wife, Holly. McClane is received by limo driver Argyle at the airport and swiftly taken to Nakatomi Plaza, where his wife’s employers have thrown a party. As the couple finally reunites at the party, McClane soon realises they are under attack. German terrorist Hans Gruber has arrived with an army of men. They have guns, bombs, and a motive: steal $640 million in bearer bonds locked behind a vault in the building. Initially, McClane’s presence in the Plaza is unknown as the off-duty cop is desperately trying to attract the attention of the outside world. When the terrorists finally realise they aren’t alone, that’s when McClane channels his inner Rambo and saves the day. Die Hard , the OG of the successful franchise, is sprinkled with Christmas nuggets. Not only do we see and feel Christmas throughout the movie, but we hear it too. There are snippets of “Jingle Bells" and “Let It Snow". There are Christmas trees and decorations all around. Not to forget, the party is held on Christmas Eve! Gruber also receives a rude Christmas surprise in the Plaza’s elevator. And, as you might have guessed, the Santa Claus “present" embodies the Christmas spirit. (20th Century Fox) Movie nerds have also noted the mention of “Christmas" at least 18 times during the blockbuster movie. During the Bruce Willis roast on Comedy Central, the Die Hard actor hilariously disagreed with the rest of the world. Willis, who played John McClane, doesn’t seem to think Die Hard is a Christmas movie. “Die Hard is not a Christmas movie, it’s a goddamn Bruce Willis movie," he asserted. Appearing on a podcast, Die Hard writer Steven E de Souza compared Die Hard with another Christmas movie – 1954’s White Christmas . He noted that both movies were released in the summer. However, Die Hard took place entirely during the Christmas holidays, while only the first and final scenes of White Christmas occurred during Christmas. The yearly bingers of Die Hard don’t think this debate carries any weight. To them, Die Hard has and always been a Christmas movie. Merriam-Webster knows what’s up. In 2018, 20th Century Studios rereleased the trailer of Die Hard with a comical emphasis on it being a Christmas movie. “He just wants to spend Christmas with the family. But when he gets stuck at the office party, it’ll be a holiday he’ll never forget," the voice-over in the trailer says. Putting an end to the raging debate, the narrator says, “This Christmas get ready to jingle some bells, and deck the halls with boughs of Holly" and then goes on to call the movie the greatest Christmas story ever told.
